headline: Vancouver's Bike Share Now Cuts More Car Trips Than Ever
meta_description: More than half of Vancouver's bike share trips now replace car journeys, with each bike cutting up to 120kg of CO₂ annually.
summary_short: Vancouver's bike share program is quietly winning at reducing emissions. More than half of trips now replace car journeys, and researchers see room to push further.
body:
More than half of Vancouver's bike share trips now replace car journeys—a milestone that shows how shared cycling can shift urban mobility away from cars.

Each bike in the system can already cut up to 120 kilograms of CO₂ emissions per year. That adds up quickly across the entire fleet, turning a convenient commute option into meaningful climate action at street level.

Researchers studying the program see the real opportunity ahead: using the existing bikes more often. The infrastructure is already there, the bikes are already deployed. The next step is simply getting more people to choose two wheels over four, one ride at a time.
quick_facts: Over 50% of Vancouver bike share trips replace car journeys
Each bike eliminates up to 120kg CO₂ annually
Researchers identify increased usage as key to deeper emissions cuts
